releasesInRange.name: pnpm 12.14.0
releasesInRange.body:
This release adds the `sideEffectsCache.exclude` setting, stops `pnpm install` from waiting on the daily update check, and keeps pnpm from aborting with a core dump when the reader of its output exits.

### Minor Changes

- Added the `sideEffectsCache.exclude` setting for packages whose build depends on something pnpm cannot include in the cache key, such as the system libraries a native addon links against. pnpm builds the listed packages in every project and never restores or saves their builds through the side-effects cache, locally or on a `remoteCache` server. Under the global virtual store, each project gets its own copy of these packages and of the packages that depend on them. Entries use the same `name`, `@scope/*`, and `name@version` patterns as `minimumReleaseAgeExclude` [#5271](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/5271).

- `pnpm login` now prints the `npm-notice` response header during web-based login. Registries use it to show the verification code that completes the sign-in in the browser.

### Patch Changes

#### Installing packages

- `pnpm install` and `pnpm add` no longer wait for the daily update check. If the command finishes first, pnpm skips the update notice and checks again next time. On a registry that accepted the connection but never answered, an install that had nothing to do used to take minutes [#16839](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16839).

- `pnpm install`, `pnpm add` and `pnpm update` now reuse `pnpm-lock.yaml` when the workspace configures a catalog entry that no dependency references, such as an unused entry or one whose package an `overrides` entry replaces. Before, every resolution in such a workspace resolved all dependencies again from the registry [#16923](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16923).

- `pnpm install` now looks up a git dependency's branch or tag once per install, even when many workspace projects depend on it. With `linkWorkspacePackages` enabled, it used to run `git ls-remote` once per project [#16899](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16899).

- A filtered install, such as `pnpm install --filter <pkg>`, now keeps the `pnpm-lock.yaml` entries of workspace projects that are missing from disk, as in a sparse checkout. Their importers, packages, and catalog entries stay even when the filter matches every project on disk [#16931](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16931).

- pnpm now decides whether a dependency that a package also declares as an optional peer is linked as a dependency or as a peer from the shallowest path that reaches the package. When an existing lockfile records such a dependency as a regular dependency and a newly added dependency now provides the peer, pnpm records it as a peer, as a fresh install does. The lockfile entry of such a package can change on the next install [#16901](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16901).

- An install that adds nothing to the store no longer changes the modification time of the store directory. CI caches that check modification 
…(truncated)

releasesInRange.name: pnpm 11.28.6
releasesInRange.body:
This release stops `pnpm publish` from sending a CI identity token to a registry it was not issued for. It also fixes installs that dropped a dependency also declared as an optional peer, and accepts empty `httpProxy` and `httpsProxy` settings again.

### Patch Changes

#### Security

* `pnpm publish` now uses an `NPM_ID_TOKEN` only if its `aud` claim matches the selected registry, such as `npm:registry.npmjs.org`. A token for another registry is skipped with a warning, and pnpm falls back to the configured credentials.

* The warning about renamed package files with invalid names no longer prints control characters from those file names.

#### Configuration

* pnpm again accepts `httpProxy` and `httpsProxy` set to `null` or written with no value in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` and the global config file, and treats them as unset. Since 11.28.5 these values failed with `ERR_PNPM_INVALID_SETTING`.

* pnpm now switches to the pnpm version a project pins even when it cannot read its configuration. Previously, a setting it rejected in the global config file, an `.npmrc` file, `_auth`, or `pnpm-workspace.yaml` stopped every command, `pnpm --version` included.

* A key under a registry URL in the `_auth` setting that does not start with `@` is now skipped with a warning, so a field a later pnpm version adds there no longer breaks this one. A key that holds an `authToken` object but lacks its `@`, such as `org` for `@org`, is still an error.

#### Resolving dependencies

* pnpm no longer drops a dependency that a package also declares as an optional peer dependency, for example `ajv` of `ajv-formats`. Since 11.28.0, in some dependency graphs the package got the dependency neither as a dependency nor as a peer, and failed to import it [#16901](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16901).

* `pnpm install` no longer fails with `ERR_PNPM_NO_MATCHING_VERSION` after a change to `overrides` when the lockfile resolves an optional peer dependency to an npm alias of another package [#16654](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16654).

* `pnpm install` and `pnpm dedupe` now link an optional peer to the workspace package that the workspace root depends on when the picked version matches it. Previously they installed the registry package with the same name and version [#16706](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16706).

* Removal overrides such as `"debug>supports-color": "-"` now also apply to an optional peer that a package declares only in `peerDependenciesMeta` [#16681](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16681).

* `pnpm dedupe` now preserves a hoisted workspace package when another package uses a separately installed peer with the same name [#16935](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16935).

* `pnpm install` and `pnpm add --config` now apply `minimumReleaseAge` when they resolve a config dependency. A config dependency range resolves to the newest version that is old enough, so a later clean `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` accepts the lockfile [#16660](https://gi
…(truncated)

prs.title: fix(fs-packlist): honor nested ignore files when `files` is set
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

With a `files` allowlist, `pnpm pack` / `pnpm publish` skipped every `.npmignore` / `.gitignore`, including ones inside listed directories. npm and pnpm 11 (npm-packlist) only skip the root ones and keep honoring nested ones within their subtree.

The packlist walk now reads subdirectories' ignore files in `files` mode. Only the root and workspace-inherited rules are replaced by the allowlist.

A file named by a `files` entry still ships even if a nested ignore file excludes it. The walk enters an excluded directory only to reach named files and keeps nothing else there, so it still never follows symlinks or leaves the package. Divergence from npm: npm keeps such a named file only when it is a direct child of the ignore file's directory (`files: ["src/util/x.test.js"]` with `src/.npmignore` = `*.test.js` drops it in npm). pnpm keeps it at any depth, which is also what pnpm 12 did before.

pnpm 11 uses npm-packlist and is not affected, so this is a v12-only fix.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#16909

fix(cli): resolve the pinned pnpm through the registry and proxy flags
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Related to https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/discussions/16911.

The report: on a network that blocks `registry.npmjs.org`, `pnpm install --registry=<azure feed>` fails with `ERR_PNPM_BAD_CONFIG_DEP: Failed to fetch metadata from https://registry.npmjs.org/pnpm`, even when the running pnpm is the version `packageManager` pins.

In that case the pre-command pass still resolves the pin, to record its integrity in `pnpm-lock.yaml`. It uses the package-manager bootstrap registry. By design, that registry reads only trusted sources and ignores the project `.npmrc` and `pnpm-workspace.yaml`. But the pass loads its own config and applied only `--config.*` overrides. It skipped the global `CliNetworkArgs` flags (`--registry`, `--https-proxy`, `--http-proxy`, `--no-proxy`), which only the main dispatch applies.

Reproduced with a dead registry URL on 12.13.0 and a fresh `HOME`:

| source | pin lookup goes to |
| --- | --- |
| `--config.registry=` | the given registry |
| `PNPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY` | the given registry |
| `registry=` in `~/.npmrc` | the given registry |
| `--registry=` | **registry.npmjs.org** (bug) |
| project `.npmrc` | registry.npmjs.org (by design, untrusted) |

After the fix, `--registry=` reaches the given registry. pnpm v11 already sends `--registry` to `packageManagerRegistries` (`CLI --registry overrides pnpm-workspace.yaml registries.default` in `config/reader/test/index.ts`), so this is v12-only.

prs.title: fix(fs-packlist): re-include the directories main, browser, and bin point into
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Closes pnpm/pnpm#16908.

pnpm 12's `fs-packlist` left out a gitignored directory during the walk and then added back only the exact `main` / `bin` file. It did not handle `browser` at all. npm-packlist, and pnpm 11 through it, adds `!/<path>` strict rules for `main`, `browser`, and `bin` after the root's ignore files. Matched partially, such a rule re-includes the ignored directory, and ignore-walk then ships everything inside it.

The walk now appends the same rules to the root's rule set. `browser` also joins the force-include and `files`-override set.

I checked the expected lists against `npm pack --dry-run` (npm 11):

| fixture | npm | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `.gitignore` `dist/` `out/`, `main` + `browser` | whole `dist/`, `out/` | same |
| `.gitignore` `dist` `out`, `main` + `bin` object | whole `dist/`, `out/` | same |
| `.npmignore` `dist/` `out/`, `main` + `bin` string | whole `dist/`, `out/` | same |
| `files: ["dist/top.js"]`, `browser: "out/browser.js"` | `dist/top.js`, `out/browser.js` | same |
| `browser` replacement map | ignored | ignored |

Two deliberate divergences, both in how the rule is built:

- npm builds the rule from the raw value, so `main: "./dist/lib/app.js"` becomes `!/./dist/lib/app.js`. That rule matches nothing, and npm drops the main file entirely. pnpm already normalizes `./` for its force-include, so the rule is built from the normalized path. The `./` and bare forms now behave the same. Paths that escape the package are still
…(truncated)

prs.title: fix(resolver): re-split lockfile-pinned children when a dependency becomes a peer
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Follow-up to pnpm/pnpm#16903. Installing in two steps could write a different lockfile than installing everything at once.

```
project
├── G > P > X      X lists B as a dependency and as an optional peer
└── O              (optional peers: P, B)
```

- **One step:** `O`'s optional peers put `P` and `B` at the project root. `X` under that `P` has `B` above it, so it takes `B` as a peer: `X(B@1.0.0)`.
- **Two steps (`G` first, then `O`):** the first lockfile records `X` with `B` as a dependency. In the second install, v12 read `P`'s children from that lockfile (pnpm/pnpm#13839 keeps them pinned to avoid churn), so `X` kept `B` as a dependency. v11 resolves the hoisted `P` fresh and writes the peer, as in one step.

**Fix:** before a newly resolved package reads children pinned by the lockfile, v12 checks whether any pinned package would now split a dependency and peer differently. If one would, it resolves the children instead of reading the pins.

The lockfile entry for `X` doesn't say `B` is also a peer, so this needs `X`'s metadata. It is read only for pinned packages with a dependency or peer whose presence above them changed. A plain reinstall reads nothing. Adding a dependency to the issue's real-world repro read the metadata of one package.

The issue's repro now writes the same lockfile in one step and in two steps, matching v11.

## Squash Commit Body

```text
A newly resolved package reads the children the prior lockfile pinned
for it (pnpm/pnpm#13839). W

prs.title: docs(resolving-deps-resolver): drop the importer-concurrency prose
fix(lockfile): reuse the lockfile when no dependency references a catalog
prs.author: Anoesj
prs.body:
## Summary

A workspace that configures a catalog entry no dependency references made every resolution resolve all dependencies again from the registry instead of reusing `pnpm-lock.yaml`. The lockfile records only referenced catalog entries, so it has no `catalogs` section in that case. Besides an unused entry, an override on a cataloged package gets there too, because it replaces the dependency's `catalog:` specifier. typescript-native-bridge documents that setup.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#16923.

### Root cause

`try_fast_update_catalogs` returned `FastCatalogUpdate::Unsupported` when the lockfile had no `catalogs` section while the workspace configured catalogs. `lockfile_reuse_seed` then withheld the reuse seed, so the walk resolved every dependency again.

### Fix

The lockfile records only the catalog entries that a dependency references, and `catalog_references_have_snapshots`, which runs first, has already checked that each reference has one. A lockfile without a `catalogs` section is therefore one whose dependencies reference none, so `try_fast_update_catalogs` now treats it as an empty one. The lockfile freshness check (`all_catalogs_are_up_to_date`) already reads a missing section that way.

pnpm 11 is not affected: the TypeScript half of pnpm/pnpm#13477, which added this fast path, already reads a missing section as empty (`lockfile.catalogs ?? {}`). The Rust port diverged, so this is a Rust-only change.

prs.author: everett1992
prs.body:

The streamed path already emits it through the reporter (pnpm/pnpm#16694), which the silent reporter drops, so both paths agree. prs.title: feat: add `sideEffectsCache.exclude` setting
prs.author: fumikun
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds a `sideEffectsCache.exclude` setting for packages whose build output depends on the environment it runs in, such as a native addon compiled against `JAVA_HOME`. Today the first successful build of such a package is stored in the side-effects cache and restored into every later project on the machine, so a project built in a different environment silently gets the first project's binary.

```yaml
# pnpm-workspace.yaml
sideEffectsCache:
  exclude:
    - java
    - '@native/*'
    - 'sharp@1.0.0 || 2.0.0'
```

A listed package is built in every project. pnpm never restores its build from the side-effects cache and never saves it there, locally or remotely. Under the global virtual store it gets a project-scoped slot. Entries use the `minimumReleaseAgeExclude` / `trustPolicyExclude` pattern syntax. The list sits in the `sideEffectsCache` object next to `read`, `write`, and `remote`; declaring only `exclude` leaves the others at their defaults, and `pnpm config delete sideEffectsCache` clears it with them. Rules match the snapshot key's structured name and version, so a bare rule also covers a git or tarball resolution whose URL contains an `@`. A `name@version` rule names registry versions only.

This implements the per-package opt-out agreed on in the issue (named `buildPolicy: no-cache` there, when settings still lived in `package.json#pnpm`). It is a new feature, so it lands in pnpm v12 only.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#5271

prs.title: fix(install): install the Windows Rust toolchain for rustup's default host
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Related to pnpm/pnpm#16854. Follow-up to pnpm/pnpm#16868.

`pnpm install` installs the Rust toolchain that `rust-toolchain.toml` names. pnpm/pnpm#16868 made the Windows toolchain ABI follow the target pnpm was built for. That was the wrong signal in two ways:

- Building pnpm for MSYS2 runs `pnpm install` on an official pnpm, which is an MSVC build, so 12.13.0 still installed `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`.
- rustup does not do this. Without a default host, `TargetTuple::from_host` in rustup's `src/dist/mod.rs` picks `{arch}-pc-windows-msvc` whatever rustup was built for. Its build target is used only when the architecture can't be detected.

On Windows the host triple now follows rustup:

| source | example |
| --- | --- |
| rustup's `default_host_triple` (`$RUSTUP_HOME/settings.toml`), taken whole when it names a supported Windows host | `rustup set default-host x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` → `x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` |
| otherwise, the MSVC toolchain for the machine's native architecture (`IsWow64Process2`, as rustup reads it) | x64 pnpm on ARM64 Windows → `aarch64-pc-windows-msvc` |

The build-target fallback from pnpm/pnpm#16868 is removed, so the toolchain no longer depends on how pnpm was built.

`MSYSTEM` is deliberately not used. Git for Windows' Git Bash also sets `MSYSTEM=MINGW64`, so it would switch most Windows developers to the GNU toolchain.

`rustup_settings_file()` moves from the CLI shim code into `pnpm-rust-toolchain` so both use one copy.

prs.title: fix(cli): stop aborting when stderr is a closed pipe
prs.author: florentdestremau
prs.body:
## Summary

When the reader of pnpm's stderr exits early, the next write pnpm makes to stderr panics in `std::io::stdio::print_to` (`failed printing to stderr: Broken pipe (os error 32)`). The release profile uses `panic = "abort"`, so pnpm dies with SIGABRT, exit code 134 and a core dump. The usual trigger is a failing script whose `[ELIFECYCLE]` line goes to a closed pipe:

```sh
# package.json: { "scripts": { "start": "sleep 1; exit 1" } }
pnpm start 2>&1 | head -1          ; echo ${PIPESTATUS[0]}   # before: 134, after: 1
pnpm start >/dev/null 2> >(true)   ; echo $?                 # before: 134, after: 1
```

This PR:

- adds `pnpm_diagnostics::eprintln!` and `pnpm_diagnostics::eprint!`, which write to stderr and drop a failed write, like the reporter already does (`let _ = writeln!(...)`);
- routes the 38 `eprintln!`/`eprint!` calls in `pnpm-cli`, `pnpm-store-dir` and `pnpm-diagnostics` through them;
- enables clippy's `print_stderr` restriction lint so the std macros cannot come back. `clippy.toml` sets `allow-print-in-tests`. Code that never ships in the pnpm binary opts out with a crate-level `#![expect]`: the `pnpm/tasks` tools, the test-only binaries of `pnpm-fs`, and the CLI e2e suite (its helpers log to stderr outside `#[test]` functions, which `allow-print-in-tests` does not cover);
- adds an e2e test that runs a failing script with a stderr pipe whose read end is already closed, and checks that the script's exit code comes back.

Fixes pnpm/pnpm#16904

prs.title: docs(pnpr): remove stale duplicated docs and fix drifted claims
fix(cli): avoid creating manifests for read-only and rejected commands
prs.author: jatmn
prs.body:
## Summary

Commands that do not write the project manifest no longer create a missing `package.json`. This covers read-only queries such as `pnpm why` and `pnpm outdated`, lockfile-only `pnpm fetch` and `pnpm sbom`, `pnpm dedupe --check`, and every command that exits with an error during argument or prerequisite validation (`pnpm rt ls`, `pnpm audit` without a lockfile, `pnpm link ./missing`, and so on). A lockfile-only SBOM reports the root component with its missing-metadata defaults instead of the initialization template. Closes pnpm/pnpm#16907.

Command state initialization keeps a missing manifest in memory as the `pnpm init` scaffold. `pnpm install` saves it after the install succeeds, `pnpm link` after every target resolved, and `pnpm add` through its existing save. Inside a workspace a missing root manifest stays an empty in-memory manifest, as before.

The lifecycle executor reads a project's manifest from disk, so a standalone project with a `binding.gyp` and no manifest would have lost its implicit `node-gyp rebuild`. The package manager writes the scaffold right before that project's `install` stage runs, which covers `install`, `update`, `dedupe`, `prune`, pnpr materialization, a `binding.gyp` created by a resolution hook, and `rebuild --pending`. `rebuild --pending` also recognizes the active project as a pending project even when its manifest is not on disk yet; it used to classify a pending entry as a project only when `package.json` existed there.

prs.title: feat(auth-commands): print npm-notice header in web login
prs.author: akushsky
prs.body:
## Summary

`pnpm login` now prints the `npm-notice` response header of the web login probe (`POST <registry>/-/v1/login`), before the login URL and QR code. The npm CLI already does this. pnpm dropped the header, so a registry that delivers a verification code through it cannot show the code to a pnpm user.

Registries such as Artifactory can return the verification code that the user compares with the code shown in the browser (the notice looks like `Verification code: 123456. Enter this code in the browser to complete the login.`). Without this change the code never reaches the terminal and the user cannot finish the login.

Behavior:

- Every `npm-notice` value of the probe response is printed through the reporter, in the order received, before the auth URL and the "Press ENTER" line.
- The text is registry-controlled, so control and formatting characters (such as bidi overrides) are removed before display. A notice that is empty afterwards is skipped. A notice never fails the login.
- Nothing is printed when the response is not successful, the body is invalid, or a URL is rejected as unsafe. A response without the header produces the same output as before.
- Only `pnpm login` is affected. The polling of `doneUrl` and the classic username and password flow are unchanged.

…(truncated)

prs.title: fix(pnpr): address audit security, immutability, and storage bugs
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:

Addresses the Section D audit security, immutability, and storage bugs identified in https://github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/131 (Related to pnpm/tasks#131):

8. **Pipeline Runs Schema Flexibility**: Remove `deny_unknown_fields` from `PublishPipelineRun` deserialization.

prs.title: fix(store): keep the store root mtime when an install adds nothing
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16929

## Problem

`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` against a complete store changed the mtime of `<store>/v11`, so GitLab CI re-archived and re-uploaded an unchanged store.

The cause is the SQLite store index. In WAL mode, SQLite creates `index.db-wal` and `index.db-shm` in the store root when a connection opens and deletes them when the last connection closes. Each step bumps the directory's mtime. Nothing else in the store changes. pnpm v9 had no SQLite index, so it didn't have this problem.

Reproduced on both the Rust CLI (12.13.0) and the TypeScript CLI (11.28.5). I snapshotted every mtime under the store before and after a frozen install, and only `v11` itself changed.

## Fix

Both CLIs now count the open connections per store root in each process (thread, for v11):

- The first connection to open records the root's mtime and its sorted entry names.
- When the last connection closes, if the entry names are unchanged, the recorded mtime is restored.
- If the root really changed (for example, `index.db` or `projects/` was created), the new mtime is kept.
- Immutable (`frozenStore`) connections create no sidecars, so they are not tracked.

Rust: `pnpm/crates/store-dir/src/store_index/root_mtime.rs`. The guard is a field of `Backend::Sqlite` placed after `conn`, so it drops after SQLite closes.
TypeScript: `pnpm11/store/index/src/rootMtime.ts`, called from the `StoreIndex` constructor and `close()`.

Notes:
- In v11, Node's `uti
…(truncated)

prs.title: feat(pnpr): support SIGTERM container shutdown and readiness probes
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Implements Section C1 (Container shutdown & readiness) of https://github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/131 (Related to pnpm/tasks#131):

1. **Graceful Container Shutdown (Unix `SIGTERM`)**:
   - `shutdown_signal` in `pnpr` listens for Unix `SIGTERM` signals in addition to `SIGINT` (Ctrl-C) using `tokio::select!`.
   - On signal receipt, the server stops accepting new connections and finishes in-flight requests, enabling clean termination with `docker stop` and Kubernetes pod stops.

2. **Storage and Auth Readiness Verification**:
   - Added `check_readiness()` across hosted storage backends (filesystem directory access and S3 bucket readiness with a 5s timeout) and cache root directories.
   - Added `check_readiness()` across authentication backends (`htpasswd` directory and file access, SQLite token store, Libsql backend, and SQLx PostgreSQL/MySQL backends).
   - Added `RegistryError::StorageUnavailable` mapping to `503 Service Unavailable`.

3. **Readiness and Liveness Endpoints**:
   - Exposed `GET /-/ready` returning `200` with `{"status": "ok", "storage": "ok", "auth": "ok"}` on success, or `503` with backend error statuses on failure.

prs.title: fix(config.reader): treat null httpProxy and httpsProxy as unset
prs.author: grzdev
prs.body:
## Summary

pnpm/pnpm#16536 started validating `httpProxy` and `httpsProxy` with `Object.hasOwn(...)` followed by `assertString`. That check also rejects `null`, so `httpProxy:` with no value, or `httpProxy: null`, in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` or the global config file fails with `ERR_PNPM_INVALID_SETTING` since 11.28.5.

`getOptionsFromPnpmSettings` now deletes a null proxy key and validates any other value as a string. A null therefore leaves the setting unset, and a proxy from `.npmrc` or the global config file still applies. If no layer sets one, the environment proxy variables apply as before. Numbers, booleans, arrays, and objects are still rejected.

v12 is not affected and already behaves this way. Its proxy overlay only replaces a key when the workspace file gives it a value, and serde reads `null` as `None`.

## Squash Commit Body

```text
`getOptionsFromPnpmSettings` validated `httpProxy` and `httpsProxy`
whenever the key was present, so a null value (a YAML key with no
value, or `null`) failed with ERR_PNPM_INVALID_SETTING. That
regressed in pnpm/pnpm#16536.

A null proxy key is now deleted and any other value is validated as a
string. Deleting it, rather than passing null through, keeps a proxy
set in a lower-priority layer (.npmrc, the global config file), which
matches v12: its proxy overlay only replaces a key when the workspace
file gives it a value.

The check lives in normalizeProxySettings so getOptionsFromPnpmSettings
stays within the size and shape limits.

prs.title: fix(cli): keep pnpm's stdio handles out of detached grandchildren on Windows
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
Fixes https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16930.

## Problem

On Windows, `pnpm nx ...` (and any `pnpm exec`/`pnpm run`) with redirected or piped output did not return while a detached grandchild, such as the Nx daemon, was still running.

## Cause

pnpm's own standard handles are inherited from the shell, so they are marked inheritable. Rust's `Stdio::inherit` gives the child an inheritable *duplicate* as its standard handle. `CreateProcess(bInheritHandles = TRUE)` also passes the inheritable originals on as stray handles. Node.js marks only its own standard handles non-inheritable at startup, so the strays travel on to the detached daemon. The shell's pipe then stays open until the daemon exits. pnpm 10 was a Node process and did the same at its own startup, so it did not leak.

## Fix

At startup pnpm marks its own standard handles non-inheritable, as Node.js does (`uv_disable_stdio_inheritance`). Children still get their stdio through the duplicates Rust creates. This is a no-op on Unix.

pnpm v11 runs on Node.js and is not affected, so this is a v12-only fix.

## Verification

- Reproduced with Nx 23.1.1 under PowerShell 7.6 and Node 24.21: `pnpm exec nx run a:hello --skip-nx-cache *> out.txt` hung until the timeout before the fix and returns after it. A minimal repro (a detached child sleeping 20s) went from about 21s to 1s.
- New Windows test `exec::exec_output_ends_while_a_detached_grandchild_runs` fails without the fix (it waits about 21s) and passes with it in under

prs.title: feat(pnpr): rate limits, request timeouts, and coalescing
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds pre-buffer authorization for package writes, upstream request coalescing (singleflight), login rate limiting, and request timeouts to pnpr.

Related to pnpm/tasks#131 (Section C3: DoS / Resource Exhaustion Protections).

- **Pre-buffer authorization**: Package write and modification endpoints (`PUT /{pkg}`, `PUT /@{scope}/{pkg}`, `PUT /{pkg}/-rev/{rev}`) check caller authentication and write permissions before reading or buffering request payloads (up to 100 MiB).
- **Upstream request coalescing (singleflight)**: Deduplicate concurrent in-flight upstream fetches (`load_upstream_packument`) for the same package and namespace so concurrent cache misses do not hammer upstream registries.
- **Login rate limiting & concurrency limits**: Throttles failed login attempts by IP and username with `429 Too Many Requests` and a `Retry-After` header. Caps concurrent login operations and concurrent package publish buffering.
- **Request timeouts**: Configurable `requestTimeout` (default 60s) layer returning `504 Gateway Timeout` when requests exceed the deadline.

prs.author: bmaurer
prs.body:
## Summary

pnpm now advertises and decodes zstd-compressed HTTP responses. The install client sends `Accept-Encoding: zstd,gzip,deflate` (previously `gzip,deflate`). reqwest decodes a zstd body before pnpm sees it.

Why: full packuments compress much better under zstd than under gzip. pnpm fetches full packuments for `trustPolicy: no-downgrade`, for `resolutionMode: time-based` on registries without a `time` field, and for `minimumReleaseAge` when the abbreviated document carries no `time`. A long field repeated across versions spans far more than gzip's 32 KB window, so gzip cannot reuse the earlier copies.

| 15 popular packages, full | 133.4 MB | 15.81 MB | 10.95 MB | 10.33 MB |
| the 14 without `vite` | 94.5 MB | 11.16 MB | 10.35 MB | 9.88 MB |
